cities.name: Marrakech
cities.tagline: The imperial red city and Morocco's main tourist hub.
cities.best: Mar-May and Sep-Nov (summer is very hot).

sights.note: Main square: storytellers, musicians and food stalls, best at sunset and night.
Maze of markets next to the square (spices, leather, lamps, carpets).
Landmark minaret beside the square. Non-Muslims see it from outside.
19th-century palace with courtyards and painted ceilings. Entry 100 MAD foreign adult (checked Nov 2026).
16th-century royal tombs. Entry 100 MAD foreign adult (checked Nov 2026).
Ruined palace with big courtyards and storks on the walls.
Old Quranic school with a carved courtyard.
Blue garden in Gueliz. 170 MAD garden only, 330 MAD with both museums, official ticket site only (checked Nov 2026).
Next to Majorelle. Book ahead.

sights.n: Day trip: Ourika Valley or Imlil
sights.note: Cool mountain air and walks, 1.5 h from the city.
Visiting the tanneries can be an interesting experience. Even if some people tell you the area is only for locals, it is possible to visit the Tanneries without paying a youngster.
If you are interested in food and eating culture, you will enjoy this museum. Audiovisual information about the rich culinary culture of Marocco, its ingredients, techniques and traditions.

Museum set in an old palace with beautiful gardens. While somewhat run-down, it is worth seeing and houses many different artifacts from Morocco through the ages, such as wood carvings, musical instruments, and weapons. Hours per Wikivoyage: 10:00–18:00.

A mixture of orchards and olive groves surrounding the water reservoir with the central pavilion which is a popular sight on tourist postcards. Not a decorative garden, and now quite run down. Price per Wikivoyage: Free admission. Hours per Wikivoyage: 09:00-17:00.

The largest Jewish cemetery in Morocco, characterized by white-washed tombs and sandy graves. The men selling tickets are full of interesting information about the cemetery but you have to ask. Price per Wikivoyage: 10 dirham. Hours per Wikivoyage: 09:00-17:00.

Synagogue which is not only a place of worship with a beautiful open courtyard, but also includes interesting displays about Judaism's varied history in Morocco, including photos of Jews in the Berber Mountains. Price per Wikivoyage: 10 dirham. Hours per Wikivoyage: 09:00-19:00 (closed Sat).
It's housed in the Dar Menebhi Palace, constructed at the end of the 19th century. Price per Wikivoyage: 50 dirham. Hours per Wikivoyage: 09:00-18:30.

In old agricultural buildings in the Palmeraie, made out of rammed earth. The architecture itself is interesting if you haven't seen it. Price per Wikivoyage: 40 dirham. Hours per Wikivoyage: 09:00-18:00?.
A museum dedicated to the renowned contemporary artist Farid Belkahia, showcasing different periods of his work Hours per Wikivoyage: Mon-Sat.
A little photography museum, it has one of the highest roof terraces in the Medina. Ticket is also valid for Museum of Mouassin Music. Price per Wikivoyage: 80 dirham.
It consists of groves of orange, lemon, fig, apricot and pomegranate trees in rectangular plots, linked by olive-lined walkways. Price per Wikivoyage: 70 dirham for foreign adults.
A very small but intricate domed pavilion, known for being the only surviving example of Almoravid religious architecture (early 12th century) in Marrakech. Price per Wikivoyage: 50 dirham.
Horse show, acrobats on Arabian horses firing rifles in the air, horseback acrobatics, belly dancing, etc. It takes place at night in a huge imitation of an old castle. Price per Wikivoyage: €15.

This is multi-use but mostly for football, with a capacity of 41,356. It's the home ground of Kawkab, who play in Botola 2 the second tier. In 2025 / 26 it hosted matches in the Africa Cup of Nations.

A 2- to 4-hour walk through the old city with a licensed local guide, covering how the souks and their crafts are organised and landmarks such as the Bahia Palace, Ben Youssef Madrasa and the Saadian Tombs. Price per Wikivoyage: US$20 per person in a small group, US$60 per person private. Hours per Wikivoyage: Morning or late afternoon, year-round.
Hours per Wikivoyage: men 12:00-13:00, women 13:00-21:00.
Hours per Wikivoyage: women 07:00-19:00, men 20:00.
Friendly staff, however, no English or French (other locals helped without any problem) Price per Wikivoyage: 12 dirham entrance, 50 dirham scrub. Hours per Wikivoyage: till 17:00.
Friendly staff, however, no English or French; other customers likely to help you out. Price per Wikivoyage: 500 dirham. Hours per Wikivoyage: Until 01:00.

stay: Medina riads: atmospheric, close to everything, can be hard to find at night (ask the host to meet you at the gate).
Gueliz (new town): modern hotels, restaurants, easy taxis.
Palmeraie and outskirts: resort hotels with pools, you need a taxi.
Riad Basma: 5 double rooms with bathroom. Price per Wikivoyage: from €35. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2019)
Dar Jaguar: Dar Jaguar is an ancient riad that has been restored as a beautiful private guesthouse. Price per Wikivoyage: From €99, breakfast included. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2018)

Riad Cinnamon: Designed and rebuilt to a very high standard with attention to detail. Unexpected extras such as the loan of a local mobile phone and ipad. Price per Wikivoyage: from £112 per room. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2017)
Riad LakLak: A riad built in the 17th century, which sleeps 12 in 2 suites and 3 bedrooms, that can be rented as a whole. Price per Wikivoyage: from €180. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2017)
Riad Melhoun: Located in central Marrakech, a 3-minute walk from the El Badi and El Bahia Palaces, it features an interior courtyard with a swimming pool and a... (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2017)
Hotel Salam (laksor): Cheap and clean hotels, doesn't seem to have showers. Price per Wikivoyage: 100 dirham for double room, no bathroom. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2017)

Dar Attajmil: Centrally located and easy to reach, Dar Attajmil has a sand colored courtyard shaded by a tall banana tree; 4 double rooms with bathroom, 1 family... Price per Wikivoyage: €80-110/night in B&B. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Riad Abaka: A spacious riad with seven beautifully furnished bedrooms and ensuite bathrooms. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Riad Chennaoui: Simple and basic riad in the Medina. The staff are friendly and happy to discuss Moroccan life and culture over a shisha in the evening. Price per Wikivoyage: Dorm beds around 100 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Riad Dar Eliane: Four spacious double bedrooms and bathrooms with A/C. Accommodation is on two floors of a restored 300 year old riad in an older quarter of... (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Riad Iaazane: A restored riad with extensive use of traditional styling and ceramics, includes a roof terrace with views. Price per Wikivoyage: Single €20, double €18, dorm €10 per person. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Riad Laksiba: £25-30 per person depending on season. A very popular Riad with UK visitors. Five bedrooms all with bespoke hand carved beds designed to be split to... (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Riad Lotus Perle: Riad Lotus Perle is in the Medina, in an old neighborhood near the lively souks and Djemaa El-Fna square, this is a wonderful riad composed of rooms... (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Riad Magellan: An elegant six-bedroom riad which offers a restful and relaxing atmosphere, in the Mouassine district. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
food: Djemaa El-Fna food stalls (prices are displayed; check drink prices before ordering)
Harira soup, tangia (a Marrakech slow-cooked meat dish), grilled meat and aubergines
Fresh orange juice stalls on the square
Chez Chegrouni on the square (vegetarian couscous, per Wikivoyage)
Eloomm: Mediterranean restaurant where slow dining meets Moroccan produce. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2025)
Black Pan: Italian restaurant. Artisanal pizzas, traditional Italian dishes and warm atmosphere. Price per Wikivoyage: Average of 100-200 dirham per dish. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2024)

Chez Yassine: Not much choice but served by very friendly people. Tajines and pizzas are great and you can also order skewers that are not on the menu. Price per Wikivoyage: 30 dirham tagines. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)

Henna Cafe: A pretty little cafe on 3 floors with an orange sign on the Berber hand-carved wooden facade opened in November 2011. Price per Wikivoyage: 40 dirham mains. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Chez Bismilah: Amazing food and wonderful service. The owner is very kind and the fantastic chef is a humble lady who cooks perfectly all the traditional Moroccan... (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Café Babouche medina: In a small street a few steps from the Jemaa El Fna square. You can eat there in a friendly atmosphere. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)

Associacion Amal: Here you can experience lunch similar to what Moroccans eat at home: this women's aid association provides women with education in exchange for food... (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Sky mabrouka: Serves the same standard fare as everywhere else in a little courtyard or terrace. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Café du Livre: A western style bookshop-café in the villa nouvelle. Price per Wikivoyage: medium priced, sandwiches ~ 40–60 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Café Kabash: Have a roof terrace with a good view. Daily Moroccan menus with tea and juice. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Diaffa: An upscale restaurant in one of the oldest buildings in the Medina, and offers Moroccan cuisine in an ambiance that recalls the Orient at the height... (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Pepe Nero: Fine Italian and Moroccan dining in gorgeous Riad. Often full so make a reservation. Price per Wikivoyage: 400 dirham for 3-4 course dinner, wine for 200. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Dar Najat's Kitchen: Daily fresh food in a boutique riad. Price per Wikivoyage: €23 per person. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2019)
Maison de la Photographie: A little photography museum, it has one of the highest roof terraces in the Medina. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
scams: If someone says a medina street is closed, ignore them. It is a known trick to lead you into a quiet alley.
Guides should show an official badge. Refuse unbadged 'helpers' who walk with you.
Taxi: insist on the meter (compteur). Petit taxi minimum is about 7 MAD in the day. If he refuses, take the next one.
Sit-down drinks on the square rarely have prices on menus. Ask first.
Solo travellers: be careful with drinks from strangers and with room service.
cities.transport: Walk inside the medina. Beige petit taxis in town (meter, max 3 passengers). Grand taxi or bus for trips out. Train to Casablanca about 2h40.

cities.name: Fes
cities.tagline: The oldest medina in use, famous for its tanneries, madrasas and craft.

sights.note: Leather dye pits. Watch from a shop terrace. Shop staff will push you to buy: be firm and polite.
14th-century madrasa, one of the religious buildings non-Muslims can enter. Entry listed around 20-30 MAD (sources differ).
Smaller but richly decorated.
Oldest university, founded 859. Non-Muslims see the gates from outside.

sights.n: Talaa Kbira street and the medina (Fes el Bali)
sights.note: Main walking street from Bab Boujloud into the old city. Green, orange and other marked walking trails exist.
Museum in an old funduq building.
Hill with the best panorama of the medina at sunset.
Fortress overlooking the old city.
Old Jewish quarter.
Former royal palace turned museum.

In the midst of the maze-like medina are the colorful leather-dying pits. Any number of young boys will offer to guide you to them: just listen for "you want to see the tanneries?" The tour is free (though it is...
Dates back to the inception of the city in the 9th century, with the completion of the foundation in 859-860. This makes it one of the oldest mosques in the world.

Southern fortress, a counterpart to the Borj Nord. The interior is not open, but like the Merenid Tombs it has spectacular views of the medina from the other side. It is a short walk (uphill) from Bab Ftouh.
The tomb of Fez's founder. Entrance is limited to Muslims, but the view from just outside its doors is still well-worth hunting down.

sights.n: Mosque and Mausoleum of Sidi Ahmad al-Tijani
sights.note: Sidi Ahmad al-Tijani is the founder of the Tijaniyya Sufi order. He was born in a Berber family in Aïn Madhi in Algeria, and died in Fez at the age of 80.
They usually have hundreds of jars of twisted root and twig neatly lined up along the walls.

The oldest garden in Fes, created by Sultan Moulay Abdallah in 18th century. It features 3000 plant species, some of them are quite rare. Price per Wikivoyage: Free admission. Hours per Wikivoyage: 09:00-20:00.
A beautiful run-down palace. Unfortunately, it has infrequent opening times, so dont count on it being accessible. Hours per Wikivoyage: 09:00-17:00.

The last major madrasa built in the medina, dating from 1670. It's less ornate than the older Marinid madrasas but larger and the dormitories of its upper stories can be visited. Price per Wikivoyage: 20 dirham.
Terrace has an incredible view over the medina if you are willing to pay 30 dirham for a glass of tea in order to access it.
This multi-use stadium is primarily used for soccer. Its two home teams are Maghreb (top tier) and Wydad de Fès (second tier). The stadium was opened in 2007 and has a capacity of 45,000.

stay: Fes el Bali riads and small hotels: best location, narrow alleys.
Ville Nouvelle: modern, near train station, quieter.
Near Bab Boujloud: easiest entrance to the medina.
Riad El Yacout: A fassi house in the medina restored on the norms and of tradition by the artisans of Fez. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)
Riad Kettani: Riad in the Medina. Has Hammam. Price per Wikivoyage: €100. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)
Riad-Boutique Borj Dhab Fez: Spa, free breakfast, wifi. Lots of Moroccan decor. Price per Wikivoyage: 332 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2020)
Dar Nour Fes: Delicious free breakfast and rooftop seating where you can look out on the medina. Price per Wikivoyage: 332 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2020)

Dar Othmane: Lovely family-run guesthouse in the heart of the medina, beautiful courtyard, roof terasse for relaxed evenings, 4 en suite rooms (single, double,... Price per Wikivoyage: from US$40 per person in a double. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2017)
Dar Fes Medina: Built in 2008. The Guesthouse features easy access and Moorish decor. Price per Wikivoyage: from US$75 per person in a double. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2017)
Camping Diamant Vert: Decent amount of shade, French toilets and (sometimes warm) showers (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
HI youth hostel: Clean, bright, friendly and well placed in the ville nouvelle. Unfortunately there is a debilitating 10PM curfew and a five hour lockout (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Hotel Cascades: The owner is hospitable and the rooms are clean, noisy and simple. Shared bathrooms on the first and second floor, free hot shower on the first. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Hotel Rex. Price per Wikivoyage: 100 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Hôtel Royal Urban Concept: Big rooms, slightly antique feeling, hot water only in the morning. Price per Wikivoyage: 378 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Hotel Volubilis: Bed bathrooms (cold shower, just over the toilet). (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Dar Bouânania: Riad-style, wonderfully decorated rooms, nice roof-terrace, wifi and very welcoming staff. Price per Wikivoyage: double 250-400 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Riad Jamai: A traditional riad that has been restored to its former slendour, with extremely helpful and welcoming staff. Price per Wikivoyage: €50-110. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
food: Bab Boujloud market streets for cheap food
Pastilla (Dar Tazi / Le Palais de Fes per Wikivoyage)
Maison Fassi, Cafe Clock (listed in Wikivoyage)
Fassi specialities: pastilla, seffa, rfissa

Bouanania: Enjoy lunch on the terrace or a leisurely dinner on the carpet-adorned second floor. Price per Wikivoyage: around 40 dirham, but prices are negotiable down. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)

La Kasbah de Fes: Friendly service, a solid selection of inexpensive Moroccan staples (excellent vegetarian tagine) and a couple of lovely high terraces overlooking... (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)

Medina cafe: Tasty and cosy café-style restaurant, however it can get too touristy. Food is fine, specially the "boricuas" (deep fried thin dough layers wrapping... Price per Wikivoyage: Mains starting at 60 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)

Chez Maimonide: Located in the home of Maimonides, the famous Jewish philosopher and rabbi. This restaurant is run by the Muslim family that now lives there, and is... (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Palais des Merinides: Table d'hote menus with basic Moroccan specialties in a very grand setting. Mediocre quality, but fabulous surroundings. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
San Remo: Fed up with couscous and tajine? Then you could try this Morocco owned Italian restaurant in the new part of town. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Dar Saada Restaurant: A favorite of Travel and Leisure magazine and is worth the indulgence. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
L'Ambre: An elegant and superior dining experience in all of Morocco. Serving up Moroccan cuisine with innovative twists, food is served in one of three... (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
scams: Fake guides: look like you know where you are going. Many 'friendly' people lead you to shops for commission.
'This road is closed' is a common lie to redirect you.
Belek! Belek! means move: a loaded donkey is coming.
Tannery: do not accept a 'free' tour that ends in a shop. Agree on any tip first.
Lone women often get harassment in alleys: stay on busier streets.
cities.transport: Walk in the medina (no cars). Red petit taxis in town. Train to Meknes, Rabat, Casablanca, Tangier.

cities.name: Casablanca
cities.tagline: Morocco's big modern city. Home of the Hassan II Mosque.

sights.note: Guided visits for non-Muslims. 140 MAD foreign adult (checked Nov 2026). Check times at the ticket office.
Seafront strip with cafes and beach clubs.
Small old town near the port.
Calm 1930s quarter with shops and pastry makers.
Hispano-Moorish building (listed in Wikivoyage).
The only Jewish museum in the Arab world (per Wikivoyage).
Many 1920s-30s buildings around Mohammed V and the Central Post Office.
Built on a rock off shore, well past The Corniche, and only accessible at low tide.
Come here to send your postcards in style! Built in 1918, the façade is composed of both round and rectangular shapes. Once you approach you will get a good view of the excellent mosaics.

This is one of the best places to see modern Morocco. Businessmen come out in droves at lunchtime to have their food in the sunshine on this modern city square. Great chances to take beautiful scenery shots too.
Run by the charity ONA, it is a place for the Moroccan art scene. Price per Wikivoyage: free of charge. Hours per Wikivoyage: Tue-Sun 09:30-19:00 (except public holidays).
21, rue Abou Mahassine Arrouyani (ex rue Boissy-d'anglas)
12, rue El Jihani
13, rue El Kaïssi
This art gallery exhibits a bizarre collection of modern welded sculptures by artists from all over Morocco.

The Association "Solidarité Féminine" has implemented an applied training program to encourage the socio-economic integration of women in single mother situations edifying employment. Price per Wikivoyage: Entrance 40 dirham. Hours per Wikivoyage: Tue-Sun 08:00-21:00, Mon 08:00-18:00.
This is multi-use but primarily for soccer. It's the usual stadium for the men's national team, and home ground for Wydad AC and Raja CA, both playing in Botola the top tier.
COSMAN Rooftop Observatory offers guided astronomy and stargazing experiences in Tit Mellil, in the Casablanca area.

stay: Centre / Maarif: central, business hotels.
Near Casa Voyageurs station: convenient for trains.
Corniche: sea views, a bit far from the centre.

Hotel Terminus: Located directly across from the Casa Voyageurs train station. The price is very high for what it is. 250 dirham for a 2-bed room with a sink. Price per Wikivoyage: 200 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)

Hotel Central: Located in the Old Medina, this simple hotel is a good budget option. The owners are friendly and have been known to give complimentary cups of mint... Price per Wikivoyage: 350 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)

Hôtel Ibis Casa Voyageurs: Excellent location right next to Casa Voyageurs train station. Excellent garden in the back, perfect for playing with kids. Price per Wikivoyage: 600 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)
Hotel Ajiad Casablanca: This central hotel has 24-hour reception, free parking and air-conditioned rooms. Price per Wikivoyage: 800 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)

Hyatt Regency Casablanca: You can choose rooms with views of Hassan II Mosque. Has a pool and several good restaurants. Live entertainment in the evenings. Price per Wikivoyage: 3300 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)

Novotel Casablanca City Center: A four-star hotel with over 200 rooms, this is a great spot for conferences and people looking for a bit of luxury. Price per Wikivoyage: 1000 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)

Atlas Airport Hotel: A modern 4-star hotel very close to the airport. This is the default accommodation for passengers with missed connections, so the price will most... Price per Wikivoyage: Double 1000 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)
Hotel Guynemer: In a time-honored building, most rooms classical style, but some rooms have been refurbished to modern style; WiFi in all rooms. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2019)
food: La Sqala (restaurant inside an old fortress, per Wikivoyage)
Patisserie Bennis Habous (famed pastries)
Seafood near the port (Taverne du Dauphin per Wikivoyage)
Spanish tapas at La Cocina (per Wikivoyage)
Le Kobe D'Or: An Asian restaurant that is hard to miss, as it has an enormous red neon sign. The inside is nicely decorated in dark red, with lots of mirrors and... (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2026)

Solidarité Féminine Association's restaurant: The Association "Solidarité Féminine" has implemented a training program to encourage the socio-economic integration single mothers. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
La Corrida: From the outside, it's easy to miss this restaurant, but look for the little sign ringed in blinking lights. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
YoSushi: Sushi is catching on in a big way in Morocco. This little place, on a side street near the prefectural police headquarters, is one of the best. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
La Table du Rétro: French cuisine. Price per Wikivoyage: 350 dirham menu. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
scams: Pickpocketing and moped bag-snatching are the main risk: hide valuables, hold your phone away from the road.
Red petit taxis: ask for the meter.
cities.transport: Tram (30 km, 49 stops). Red petit taxis. Train from Casa Voyageurs to Rabat, Marrakech and Fes. Al Boraq high-speed train to Tangier.

cities.name: Rabat
cities.tagline: Calm capital with a UNESCO medina, kasbah and royal sites.

sights.note: Blue-and-white old fort with views over the river and sea.

sights.n: Hassan Tower and Mohammed V Mausoleum
sights.note: Unfinished 12th-century minaret and royal tomb.
Roman and Merenid ruins with storks. Entry about 70 MAD general (sources differ; one reports 30 self-guided).
Calmer than other medinas.
Mint tea over the sea (listed in Wikivoyage).
Older, narrower medina across the river.
Large colourful seaside cemetery.

The Kasbah is the oldest part of Rabat. It has narrow streets with cute white and blue houses, the Andalucian Gardens, the Oudaias Museum housed in a 17th century palace, and a great view of the Atlantic Ocean. Price per Wikivoyage: Free entrance.
Rather small and not particularly appealing one. There are a couple of rustic cafes. Also surfing gear is available for rent here.
This museum houses artifacts from various periods of Morocco's history, including ancient Roman and medieval objects. Hours per Wikivoyage: As of November 2019 closed for restoration.

sights.n: The Currency Museum of the Bank Al-Maghrib
sights.note: Angle Avenue Allal Ben Abdellah et Rue Al-Qahira
The city's own beautiful art-deco cathedral.
It is huge, you cannot really visit it (but it is a nice walk), the armed guards might allow you walk from one entrance to another especially if you look like a tourist. Bring your passport.
One of the old city's best medieval gates, located close to downtown and the Royal Palace. Price per Wikivoyage: Free.

Contains more than 100 species of Moroccan, Saharan and other African animals in open spaces simulating their natural habitats (mountains, desert, savanna and rain forest). Price per Wikivoyage: 50 dirham, students 35 dirham. Hours per Wikivoyage: 10:00-17:30.

A small but very pretty 14th-century madrasa (college), located next to the city's Grand Mosque. The mosque is closed to non-Muslims, but the madrasa can be entered. It is similar in style to the madrasas of Fez. Price per Wikivoyage: Around 60 dirham.
Theatre in Downtown Rabat, nothing absolutely outstanding but there are performances each month.

stay: Ville Nouvelle near the station: easy and central.
Medina: budget hotels.
Agdal: modern, quiet.

HI Hostel Rabat: A youth hostel on the edge of the medina walls. Four large dorm rooms with 16 bunks. A 10-minute walk from the train station. Breakfast is included. Price per Wikivoyage: 65 dirham per bunk. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2018)
Hotel Majestic. Price per Wikivoyage: 285 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2018)
Hôtel Majliss. Price per Wikivoyage: From €70. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2018)
Villa Mandarine: Set in an exotic orange grove hidden away from the hustle and bustle of the city, quite expensive. Price per Wikivoyage: From €150. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2018)

Hotel Splendide: In the Ville Nouvelle, an easy walk from the train station. Large rooms and big windows, lots of light, around a central courtyard. Quiet and clean. Price per Wikivoyage: 100 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2017)
Hotel de la Paix: Dingy and dank. If you don't get a room with an en suite shower, you don't get to take one at all. Price per Wikivoyage: 150 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2017)

Medina Surfing Association: Hostel in an old home in the Medina. Comfortable, free breakfast and occasional dinners on the terrace. 150 dirham per person. Price per Wikivoyage: From €13. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2017)

Hotel Central: Bright room with shower and sink, toilet outside. 10-minute walk to Medina. 2-minute walk from Rabat Ville Train Station. Next to main street Ave. Price per Wikivoyage: 120 dirham single. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Hôtel Balima: 3-star hotel. Closed for renovation as of Jan 2018. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Hotel Sofitel Jardin Des Roses: 5-star hotel close to the Royal Palace and a park, considered by some the best (and one of the most expensive) hotel in the city. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Golden Tulip Farah Rabat: 192 rooms on the banks of the Bourgreg river. Practically within the city centre, next to some of the most recognized monuments within Rabat: the... Price per Wikivoyage: From 1796 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
food: Sandwich and fish stalls near the medina
Cafe Maure at the Kasbah
Le Petit Beur for bstilla (listed in Wikivoyage)
Majestic: A Cafe (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Pizza des Gourmets (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Dar Naji Agdal (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Le P'Tit Resto: Cafe and sandwich shop with lunch specials and desserts. 35 dirham for a sandwich. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Mega Mall Food Court: Free Wi-Fi hotspot. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
La Mamma’s Pizza: One of the oldest pizzerias in town. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Ya Mal Al-Sham: Syrian restaurant (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Patisserie La Comedie: Fancy pastries. Croissants 4 dirham. Ice cream 6 dirham per scoop. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Ty Potes (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Villa Mandarine: Considered as one of the best restaurants in the city (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Paul: Traditional French bakery that serves as a restaurant. Can be quite pricy, but the food is magnificent. Worth a visit for their olive bread. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Matsuri (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Café Weimar (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
scams: Rabat is considered safe. Normal care with valuables.
Blue petit taxis: ask for the meter.
cities.transport: Tram between Rabat and Salé (about 6 MAD in 2019, check now). Blue petit taxis. Train station Rabat Ville in the centre.

cities.name: Tangier
cities.tagline: Port city where Africa meets Europe, with medina, cafes and Cap Spartel.

sights.note: Narrow alleys and the Kasbah Museum in the former sultan's palace.
The two old squares that join the medina to the new town.
Famous cliff cafe with sea views (listed in Wikivoyage).

sights.n: Caves of Hercules and Cap Spartel
sights.note: Coast west of the city where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean.
First US diplomatic property abroad (listed in Wikivoyage).
14th-century traveller born in Tangier.

A large mosque built in the 17th century, with its minaret rising above the city walls towards the sea. It's not the first place of worship on that place, before the mosque there has been a cathedral and a Roman temple.

The "small market" was at one point one of the greatest market places in Morocco. In the early 20th century which was the heyday of the city, wealthy people settled in the area around petit souq, and with them came...
Built by the Spanish in the 1870s in modernist style, this is the main place of worship for Tangier's Christian community.
An art museum, or maybe rather an archive related to the history of Tangier opened in 1930 in a former synagogue. In addition to art, there are newspapers, photographs and posters on display.
A large lively park-like square just southwest of the medina. Next to it there's the Sidi Bou Abib Mosque.
Built in 1917 and decorated with polychrome tiles, this is the mosque right next to the grand socco.
After the first Anglican church got too small, the current one was built behind the Sidi Bou Abib mosque. The church is built in Moorish style and the belltower is shaped like a minaret.
The continuation of the grand socco to the west, this garden features a large marble fountain and park benches.
Closed and falling to pieces but take a photo from outside the gates as you pass by on the way up to the Grand Socco.
Museum showcasing Moroccan modern art, mostly traveling exhibitions.
This impressive building is nowadays a government-owned residence for visitors. Until 1990 it served as a museum of historical battles with statues of soldiers on different battlefields.
Built by the Spanish (who else?) in the 1940s, this is the last remaining bullring in Morocco.
A great place for watching the sunrise and experiencing North African countryside.
Aquatic park with a tremendous view of the coast. Open in 2005 it costs €5 for children and €10 Adults has aqua slides, karting circuits, café, romantic restaurant with excellent pancakes.
Completed in 2011, this stadium is multi-use but primarily for soccer, with a capacity of 75,500. The home team is IR Tanger, playing in Botola Pro the top tier.
Jazz festival with artists from all over the world performing. It comprises both large outdoor concerts at large squares in the city and smaller ones at indoor locations. Held yearly.

stay: Medina and Kasbah: riads and small hotels.
Ville Nouvelle / near Place de France: central.
Near the corniche: sea view.
Magellan Hotel: Quiet and very basic, hot showers, has a garage for your car or motorcycle, and costs 150 dihams/night w/20 dirham for parking. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
Camping Miramonte: Reputedly the best campsite, also offers bungalow accommodation. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)

Hotel Continental: This hotel, situated in the medina and within easy reach of the port, is very much in the 'former glory' category, with past guests including Degas,... Price per Wikivoyage: 365-420 dirham for a double. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
Hotel Shehezerade: On the beachfront, clean and comfortable, cheap and cheerful (€30-35). (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
Hotel Solazure: On the beachfront but caters mostly to package tourists. Poor service and not particularly clean or cheap. €50-60 (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
Hotel Marco Polo: Clean, modern and decent sized rooms with air conditioning and satellite television. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
Hotel Ramada Encore Tanger: On beachfront — 4-star hotel. Modern and reasonably priced with sea facing rooms. Price per Wikivoyage: €80–100. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
Hotel Mövenpick: Expensive but modern luxury hotel with an adjoining Casino. 5-star hotel. Price per Wikivoyage: €160-180. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
Hotel El Minzah: Decor is traditional Moroccan arabesque. This is the most famous 5-star hotel in Tangier. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
Hotel Omnia el Puerto: Not on the beachfront but is clean and comfortable 4-star hotel. Price per Wikivoyage: €70–80. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
Hotel Intercontinental: Good service and clean. Not part of the Intercontinental chain. Price per Wikivoyage: €50-70. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
Hotel Le Mirage: This is a 5-star hotel on the Atlantic coast, with a kilometer of clean beach. It is a little far from Tangier and an ideal secluded spot. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
Hotel Rif: Renovated 5-star hotel on the beachfront. Famous former guests include Winston Churchill and Jean Claude Van Damme. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)

Hotel Royal: Right up the hill from the port entrance, on the way up to the medina. Rooms with a shared bath start around 120 dirham but it was easily talked... (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
food: Seafood in the port (see Wikivoyage)
Local cafes: cafe au lait is cheaper in places where locals sit
Street snacks and fresh orange juice

Restaurant Darna (de L'association Darna): The Darna organization helping women and children in difficulties is operating a restaurant, popular among the western expats in the city. Price per Wikivoyage: Daily four-course menu 60 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Restaurant Ahlen: Moroccan cuisine served in a modest restaurant, a popular suggestion of several nearby accommodations. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Abou Tayssir: A Syrian restaurant (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Chez Hassan Bab Kasbah (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Riad Al Andalous Restaurant: Moroccan cuisine (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Bocadillo Abdelmalik: Fast food. A fabulous and cheap sandwich of kefta, egg, fries on a baguette at around 14 dirham (June 2015) (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Oslo Pizza: Pizzas and snacks. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Sandwich City (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Eric's Hamburger 1 (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Sandwich Les Quatre Saisons (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)

Café à l'Anglaise: In the heart of the Kasbah on the highest peak of the Medina of Tangier with panoramic views, It has a range of veggie meals and all dishes are... Price per Wikivoyage: €8 (Dec 2015). (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)

Saveurs de poissons - Chez Poppeye: Excellent seafood and fish restaurant, served with some kind of couscous and tajine as is typical in Morocco. Fruit juice is also a speciality. Price per Wikivoyage: 100­-150 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
Le Pagode: Chinese and Vietnamese restaurant with pleasant decor and friendly service. The food has received mixed reviews. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
Otori Sushi: According to many reviewers the best Japanese food in Tangier, especially sushi. Price per Wikivoyage: about 120 dirham/person. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
scams: Hustlers are common at the port and in the medina. Say a firm 'la, shukran' and keep walking.
Arriving by ferry: people offering to fill your immigration form want money. Do it yourself.
Check the exchange rate yourself before changing euros.
cities.transport: Walk in the medina. Blue and white petit taxis. Al Boraq high-speed train to Casablanca (about 2h17 in Nov 2026 timetable).

cities.name: Chefchaouen
cities.tagline: The blue mountain town in the Rif. Slow, walkable and photogenic.
cities.best: Spring and autumn. Nights are cold in winter.

sights.note: Walk the blue alleys. Go early morning for empty streets.

sights.n: Outa el Hammam square and Kasbah
sights.note: Main square with the old kasbah and Grand Mosque.
Waterfall and spring at the edge of the medina where locals gather.
Hill walk for the sunset view of the town.
Day hike in Talassemtane National Park. Needs a grand taxi from town.
The oldest mosque (built in 1475-76) and the main historic Friday mosque of Chefchaouen. Off limits to non-Muslims.
It's the second-oldest residential agglomeration of the houses of old Andalusian families. There are a large number of shops and stalls that sell local products.
Small square with a traditional fountain in the middle.

A rarely used mosque overlooking the town from a hill behind Ras El Ma. It was built by the Spanish in the 1920s and is now a popular sunset view point. There is a trail leading to another mosque — further uphill.
Smallish museum showcasing fauna and flora of Talassemtane National Park. Introduces the park itself as well as provides with hiking maps. Price per Wikivoyage: Free admission.

A good viewpoint on the town and the valley, especially on sunsets. It can be reached from the south gate of the medina (Bab el-Ain) by climbing the road coasting the medina on the west side until the east gate (Bab...
Easy 40 min, 2 km (one way) hike.
Moderate 6 km (one way) hike.
Run by a tremendously approachable man called Hassan, it can be found towards the eastern end of the medina, between the old olive tree and the waterfall. Hours per Wikivoyage: 09:00-18:00-ish.
Can organise pottery and gastronomy workshops.

stay: Medina guesthouses and riads: best atmosphere.
Near Bab el-Ain: easy bus and taxi access.
Book ahead mid-July to September.

Dar Antonio: Nice guesthouse right in the Medina. Clean and quiet with a great view on the top floors. Hot water on demand. Shared facilities. Price per Wikivoyage: Double 330 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)
Harmony Hotel: Good value for solo travellers, who pay less but still get double beds. Price per Wikivoyage: Room 80 dirham per person, 250 dirham double. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)

Hotel Andaluz: A popular little budget hotel with a nice rooftop terrace and cool (occasionally damp if on the ground floor) rooms. Price per Wikivoyage: Double 150 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)
Hotel Ouarzazate: In the medina is a decent choice with a good location. Price per Wikivoyage: From 160 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)
Hostel Aline: A nice, clean place; catch it during low season and you'll likely end up with a room to yourself. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)
Pension Cordoba: Very friendly staff, nice welcoming rooms and a big and comfy roof terrace. Price per Wikivoyage: 170 dirham per double room. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)
Pension la Castellana: It has a central courtyard and roof terrace. Price per Wikivoyage: Room 80 dirham per person. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)

Casa Perleta: Inside the medina (Bab Souk entrance), freshly renovated. Most rooms have en suite bathrooms. Run by native Spanish speakers. Price per Wikivoyage: Double from 550 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)

Dar Meziana: A beautiful riad carefully decorated by the owners, giving each bedroom an individual character full of warmth and beauty. Price per Wikivoyage: Double from 700 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)
Dar Rass El Maa: A charming guest house below the spring. Price per Wikivoyage: From 490 dirham (singles). (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)

Dar Lbakal Guesthouse: Guesthouse with a unique interior, a charming and artistic furniture and amazing scenery that you can enjoy while relaxing on the terrace. Price per Wikivoyage: From 500 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)
Hotel Madrid: Great service staff, always willing to help. They have maps and can give information on the town. Price per Wikivoyage: 500 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)
Hotel Parador. Price per Wikivoyage: From 650 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)

Hostel Gernika: Inside the medina, very clean, luminous rooms. Has shared showers, with lots of hot water. Some rooms ensuite. Price per Wikivoyage: Double room 350-450 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)
food: Local breakfast of eggs, cheese, olives and tea
Baghrir pancakes with honey
Fish tagine (Chez Foad, Granada in Wikivoyage)
Baissara (pea soup)
Chez Aziz snack: For a sandwich break, head for the local sandwich dealer to the left of Bab el-Ain gate. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)
Cafe Restaurant Sofia: Excellent traditional soup (only 10 dirham!), beef and couscous, and vegetable tagine. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)
Restaurant Triana: Mainly European cuisine. Live concerts in the evenings. Open terrace with mountain views. Price per Wikivoyage: 150-200 dirham per meal. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2023)

Assadaa: This little restaurant occupies both sides of the street, with tables on the road, under a tree, and on a roof terrace. Price per Wikivoyage: Lunch for 50 dirham, all included. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Restaurant Populaire Bab Ssour: Good food in a quiet room with a friendly owner. Many languages spoken. Good local cheese. Price per Wikivoyage: 50 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)

Cafe Clock: Cult cafe chain from Fes run by European. It occupies an entire four-floor riad, it has a roof-top terrace, nice atmosphere. Price per Wikivoyage: 50-80 dirham per meal. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)

Restaurant Hamsa: Meeting point for younger people. Great view from the terrace which overlooks central square and mountains. Food is average. Price per Wikivoyage: From 50 dirham per plate. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Mandala: Pizza, pasta, salads. Small European-alike pizzeria. OK-ish quality, eastable. Price per Wikivoyage: 50 dirham per plate. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Chez Hicham: Long waiting time, average food, great view over the main square. Price per Wikivoyage: 65 dirham tajines. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
scams: At the bus station, touts may say your hotel is closed or full. Check yourself by phone.
Overbooked hotels sometimes move you to another for commission.
Offers of hashish are illegal for you. Walk away.
cities.transport: Everything in town is on foot. CTM and other buses from Fes, Tangier, Tetouan. Grand taxis to Akchour.

cities.name: Essaouira
cities.tagline: Windy fortified port town: relaxed, with fresh fish and art.
cities.best: Spring to autumn. Wind is strong in summer.

sights.note: Sea ramparts with old cannons. Entry about 60 MAD (checked Nov 2026).
Small walkable medina with art galleries and woodwork shops.
Fresh fish sold at the dock.
Kitesurf and windsurf. Water is cold, wind is strong.
Walk south along the beach.
No description in the source yet. Check locally before you go.
Price per Wikivoyage: 60 dirham for foreigners. Hours per Wikivoyage: 09:00-17:00.
It's a nature reserve, and thus can't be visited without an official authorization. In the 19th century, it was used as a quarantine station for pilgrims returning from Mecca.

is at the south end of Essaouira's beach, and is allegedly where Jimi Hendrix once spent some time. Even if the stories aren't true, this long, windswept beach with its ruined fort is a fantastic walk.

Guided eco-friendly tours of the amazing countryside around Essaouira. You can discover the Argan Woods, the Thuya Forests, and the Dunes, take mint tea in a Berber village, and learn the secrets of a unique ecosystem... Hours per Wikivoyage: half day.
In June.
Kitesurf, surf and windsurf directly on the main beach. Recent equipment.
A mix of art and spa, as per the name. Patrons can enjoy viewing art while having spa treatments.

stay: Medina riads: small and calm.
Near the beach: sea views, windy.
Touts at the bus station offer cheap rooms: check the place first.
Hotel Palais Des Remparts: Luxury Hotel Essaouira. Price per Wikivoyage: Singles/doubles start at. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2017)
Riad Dar Nafoura-Mogador: Beach, free breakfast, free high speed internet (WiFi), 9 rooms. Price per Wikivoyage: 290 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2017)
Essaouira Lodge: Luxury hotel residence, outside of town, with high-end hotel service, including shuttle. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2016)
Hotel Orson Welles: Good hotel and good price with free parking facing the hotel. Price per Wikivoyage: 400 dirham for double room with breakfast. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)

Riad Lunetoile: 200-year-old family home with a beautiful terrace giving a breathtaking view of the Atlantic Ocean, the bay and Diabet in the distance, as well as a... Price per Wikivoyage: from €35, see website or call for special offers. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
Sofitel Essaouira Mogador Golf & Spa: Right on the beach, it will be happy to indulge your every whim, for a hefty price. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)

Riad Bab Essaouira: 4 ensuite accommodations in a designed riad with sub-Saharan African vibes. 2 roof terraces with a fantastic ocean view at 360. Price per Wikivoyage: €85. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)
Essaouira Wind Palace: A few meters from the port, the beach, Skala, the place and the souks. Restored in authentic Arab-Andalusian style. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Villa Maroc (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Dar 91: Private, self-contained house with its own roof terraces, in the walled old town. The house is a chilled-out and authentic ‘home from home’, which is... (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Dar Lazuli: 200-year-old riad. Price per Wikivoyage: £60 per night. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Dar Leila: Restored, staffed riad sleeping up to 10 in the heart of the medina. It has 5 beds, 3 baths and a secluded roof terrace. Price per Wikivoyage: From £500 per week. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Dar Zahira: Relaxed retreat hidden in one of the medina's narrow alleys. The small riad is built around a courtyard and sleeps a maximum of 6 persons. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Riad de la Mer: Very large 18th century riad, retaining original features and character. Stunning views of the ocean, centrally located just off the main square, 5... Price per Wikivoyage: £47.50. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
food: Grilled fish at the port stalls (pick your fish, agree the price first)
Argan oil products from women's cooperatives
Seafood tagine
Berber Cafe: Small friendly cafe, seats about 8 for meals and decor is mainly old boxing posters (husband used to coach), but the small menu is good and the... (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2017)
Patisserie Driss: A great place for cakes and snacks. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2015)

Fish Market: If you are a fish enthusiast, you should not miss the food in the market. Buy your fish (cheap, shrimps are 50 dirham/kilo, sardines 5-6 dirham) take... Price per Wikivoyage: buy the fish + 25 dirham for the baking. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Chez Omar: Small street with restaurants that serve great and cheap food in huge quantities. If you order fish they buy it fresh from the market. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
La Decouverte: If you are tired of tagines, disappointed by Italian-Moroccan pasta, give La Decouverte a try. Price per Wikivoyage: Mains 50-80 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Shyadma's Vegan Food: Lovely vegan/vegetarian spot in the middle of Place El Khayma, a less visited place with many restaurants. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
scams: Fake 'hash brownies' sold near the square. Illegal and often fake.
Bus-station touts offering cheap riads: do not follow without checking.
cities.transport: Walk in the medina. Taxis cost a flat small fare in town (8 MAD day per Wikivoyage Jan 2024). Supratours and CTM buses to Marrakech and Agadir.

cities.name: Agadir
cities.tagline: Big beach resort in the south with sun nearly all year.

sights.note: Long wide beach.
Ruined fortress on the hill with city and sea views.
Berber crafts (listed in Wikivoyage).
Large covered market.
Surf village and river pools 20-30 min away.
The museum which exhibits a small collection of Berber objects from 18th and 19th century the likes of old Berber music instruments, Berber jewelry, traditional clothing and old manuscripts.
The sign is missing: you go through iron gates on the corner. Mostly photographic exhibits which concentrate on the Agadir earthquake on 29 February 1960.
Coco Polizzi has been recreating a traditional Moroccan Medina on route N1 in Bensergao. Price per Wikivoyage: 40 dirham.

There's part of the original fortress which is at the top of the hill beside the city, over the huge painting. It's possible to walk up there, taxi will cost 30-50 dirham. Price per Wikivoyage: Free admission.

Imesouane, Devils rock (at the town of Tamragh and with the neighbouring towns of Aourir and Taghazout), Anchor point, Cro-Cro and many others. There are a lot of surf schools and surf camps and surf shop.

This is a small zoo, called "Vallée des Oiseaux" ('Birds Valley'). There is a very nice cage you can walk inside, many birds from all the world, some goat-like animals from the Atlas, and even exotic mammals. Price per Wikivoyage: Free.
With three top-notch golf courses, Agadir can rival most countries' golf facilities. Ask at any large hotel about the bus transport which collects visitors several times a day.
This is multi-use but mostly for soccer, with a capacity of 45,480. The home team is Hassania Agadir, playing in Botola Pro the top tier. In 2025 / 26 it hosted matches in the Africa Cup of Nations.

stay: Beachfront hotels and resorts.
Talborjt: cheaper hotels (per Wikivoyage).
Taghazout: surf hostels.
Residence Fleurie: This is a nice cheapie downtown with private balconies, pool, a/c, wifi, free breakfast, and kitchenettes. Price per Wikivoyage: 369 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2020)
Hotel Diaf: If you're on a budget this hotel is a great place to stay. It's near where the bus stops (1 min walk), right next to an internet cafe and about 20... (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2019)
Hotel Tamri: Cheap place to stay. Hot shower outside - from 07:00-10:00 morning and 18:00-21:00. Price per Wikivoyage: 100 dirham for a single room. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2018)
Anezi Hotel Agadir: The hotel has a commanding position with a magnificent view of the bay and the city. Price per Wikivoyage: From 700 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2018)

Atlas Kasbah Ecolodge: 20 minutes from Agadir, this ecolodge is the perfect place to discover centuries-old Berber culture and the UNESCO Argan Biosphere Reserve. Price per Wikivoyage: From 700 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2018)
Hotel Petit Suede: Close to the centre, rooms with shower (shared toilet), very clean, breakfast served in a rooftop eatery. Street-facing rooms can be a bit noisy. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2017)

Hôtel Timoulay & Spa Agadir: 10 minute walk from the beach. This hotel is on the smaller side, but the rooms are clean and spacious. Price per Wikivoyage: US$100-200. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2017)
Hotel Sud Bahia: Four-storey with 246 rooms 400 meters from the beach in the center of Agadir and with an outdoor pool. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
food: Fresh fish near the port
Cheap restaurants in Talborjt
Argan and amlou
Herguita: Fantastic location with view of the ocean. Typical, good food. Best brochette. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
K-moon: Small restaurant with excellent grilled meat over a wood fire and lots of small bowls filled with different things. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Rotisserie Al Marché شواية المارشي: If you're looking for a Moroccan street food experience, this one is for you. Authentic place. Best sandwiches. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
L'étoile d'Agadir: Friendly and typical restaurant, traditional cuisine. A lot of nostalgia in this place. Very good restaurant with local specialties. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Restaurant les trois chaudrons: Homemade Moroccan taste. Very good welcome and nice service. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Restaurant du Port de Pêche (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Le Flore (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Café Del Mar (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Ô Playa (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Rituel (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Pure Passion (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
scams: Taxi: use the meter in petit taxis.
Beach vendors and quad offers: agree prices first.
cities.transport: City buses (small fare). Petit taxis. Supratours and CTM buses to Marrakech, Essaouira and the south.

cities.name: Meknes
cities.tagline: Imperial city of Moulay Ismail: big gates, calmer than Fes.

sights.note: Largest and most striking of the city gates.
Square between the medina and the imperial city.
Free to enter, non-Muslim access limited, check hours.
Huge granaries and stables of Moulay Ismail.
Madrasa with a rooftop view. Fee about 60 MAD in Wikivoyage 2018, check.
Entry 100 MAD foreign adult (checked Nov 2026).
Holiest town in Morocco, hillside views.
Redone with new brickwork, this square once rivaled Djemaa el Fna in Marrakech but is now significantly less exciting (though there are a few nice cafés and snack spots in which to people-watch).

The former palace gardens, now converted into a golf course. This place is absolutely marvelous. The gardens are beautifully kept and it is entirely surrounded by palace walls. It is open to the public.
A huge underground prison where Moulay Ismail allegedly kept prisoners. A little pricey for basically just some empty halls underground. Price per Wikivoyage: 60 dirham.
Basin built at the time of Ismail Moulay in the imperial city, northwest of the granaries.
Closed to non-Muslims.
Meknes' largest and oldest standing mosque (note: Non-Muslims are not permitted to enter).

This old palace, now a museum, is at the back of Place Hedim. It now houses a very nicely designed local heritage museum, mainly about music with many instruments on exhibition. 30 Dirham. Hours per Wikivoyage: Wed-Mon 10:00–17:30.

Borj Belkari is an Alaouite bastion built in the 17th century as a part of the famous Ismaili wall created by Sultan Moulay Ismail (1672-1727), it played an important role in the defensive system of the city.
There is a very popular public swimming pool between the medina and the new city, on a hot day it is a godsend.

stay: Ville Nouvelle hotels near the train station.
Medina riads for atmosphere.

Riad ma Bohème Chez Amal et David: Homey guest house with wifi and nuptials. Really close to Lahdim Square and the other Medina attractions. Price per Wikivoyage: 249 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2020)
Riad Yanis: Economical and good breakfast. Close to Medina attractions. Price per Wikivoyage: 212 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2020)
Ibis Meknes: A stylish hotel with pool and appealing dining within walking distance of the Medina. Price per Wikivoyage: 320 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2020)
HI-affiliated youth hostel: Wedged between the medina and ville nouvelle, just two doors down from the much swankier and well known Hotel Transatlantique. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2018)
Hotel Majestic: Renovated, the Majestic offers a lovely garden as well as clean and nice rooms overlooking the most busy avenue in Meknes. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Riad Atika: Guest house in the old Medina with 14 rooms and a beautiful terrace. Price per Wikivoyage: 330-825 dirham incl. breakfast. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Riad Hiba: Beautiful guest house in the old city (Medina) with 7 rooms. Price per Wikivoyage: 385-649 dirham incl. breakfast. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Riad Idrissi: Guest house in the old Medina with 12 rooms and a beautiful terrace. Price per Wikivoyage: 440-605 dirham incl. breakfast. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Palais Didi: A restored old palace/riad in the medina right by a palace wall. Maison d'hotes - restaurant. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Ryad Bahia: The first riad to open in Meknes, its owners, and most of the staff, speak English and are extraordinarily helpful in arranging tours and the like. Price per Wikivoyage: 650 dirham per single or double. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Riad Felloussia: Open daily. A traditional home in the heart of the medina. Great view of El-Hedim square. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Rue Antsirabe for cheap Moroccan staples (Wikivoyage lists Ville Nouvelle restaurants)
Les Colliers de Colombe: Delicious Moroccan staples, including the must-try pastilla. Price per Wikivoyage: Most dishes are over 100 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2026)

Miam's Food (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)

Riad d'Or (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)
Restaurant Palais Ismailia (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2022)

Petit taxis: ask for the meter.

cities.name: Ouarzazate
cities.tagline: Gateway to the Sahara and Morocco's film studio town.
cities.best: Spring, autumn and winter. Summer is very hot.

sights.note: Old kasbah. Entry about 20 MAD (checked Nov 2026).
Film studio tour. About 60 MAD (one source, Nov 2026).
UNESCO ksar used in many films. See that page.
Palm oasis near town, by grand taxi.
Scenic road south to Zagora via kasbahs.
Not that exciting and many items are not marked or signed, but a good alternative if you do not want to head out of the city to the other museums/studios. Price per Wikivoyage: 30 dirham.
Former synagogue turned into some kind of museum. Rooms filled with items, but almost no descriptions. Guided tour only. Admission is "voluntary".
You might wonder what is that huge tower looming over the hills next to the city, which can be seen from dozens of miles around Ouarzazate going along the highway.

CLA Studiosis along the same road as Atlas Studios about a km closer to Marrakech. The Atlas Studios tour is mostly TV movies and The Mummy Returns remake. The sets are unconvincing in person. Price per Wikivoyage: 100 dirham. Hours per Wikivoyage: 8:30AM to sunset.

stay: Hotels along Avenue Mohammed V and near the main square.
Kasbah-style guesthouses outside town.

La Palmeraie: Not the most beautiful and best rated hotel, but centrally located, and they have good offers sometimes, which includes a swimming pool, breakfast,... Price per Wikivoyage: 340 dirham for a double. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2019)

La Gazelle: Clean, cheap hotel, safe parking in the courtyard, ATM just next door, bakery across the road. Price per Wikivoyage: 156 dirham double room with hot shower. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Hotel Amlal: Simple and clean hotel located right on the town center. This is a nice cheap option and great quality price and facilities. Price per Wikivoyage: 1 person 200 dirham, 2 persons 250 dirham, 3. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Zaghro Hotel: It is located a bit far from the village but is neat and clean, has a restaurant and a pool to enjoy after some time in the desert. Price per Wikivoyage: €7-20 per person with breakfast included. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Hotel Royale: In the centre, has ugly rooms. It can get very cold in winter, and the street facing rooms are very noisy. Price per Wikivoyage: triple room 160 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Hotel el Salam: Not bad for budget people, however cold in the night. Price per Wikivoyage: 70 dirham for single room with hot shower. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Hotel la Vallée: Offers accommodation, restaurant service, swimming pool, Moroccan caidal tent party lounge, tours and organized excursions in Morocco and 4wd/ATV... Price per Wikivoyage: €20-30 per person with breakfast and dinner. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Dar Rita: New riad in Ouarzazate located on the typical district of Tassoumate near the river bank and palm trees. Price per Wikivoyage: Double room w. half board: €70. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
I Roccha: Extremely friendly hosts and international mix of travellers. Quiet and relaxing place overseeing a valley in a small village of Tisselday. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Hotel Yasmina. Price per Wikivoyage: 300 dirham. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
Dar Ahlam: 10-room hotel in Skoura, about 40 km from Ouarzazate. Expensive, but distinctive in every element: architecture, style, service, and food. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)

Riad Ksar Ighnda: On the edge of the desert, the Riad Ksar Ighnda opens its doors onto the Atlas Mountains. Authentic yet modern setting. Price per Wikivoyage: ~€100-240. (Wikivoyage listing, check before you go)
food: Cheap restaurants on Mohammed V
Saffron-flavoured tea in the Ouarzazate area (Wikivoyage)

Aït Benhaddou: ignore anyone claiming a 'fee' to enter the bridge.
cities.transport: Petit taxis (low fares). CTM buses from Marrakech (about 4-5 h). Airport with flights.

Great views, free (Wikivoyage).
Earthen villages along the road.

cities.name: Merzouga
cities.tagline: Sahara dunes of Erg Chebbi, camel treks and desert camps.

sights.n: Erg Chebbi dunes at sunrise or sunset
sights.note: Walk or camel trek into the dunes.
Camp stay with dinner and music. Budget camps from about 150-350 MAD per person (one source, Aug 2026).
Birds, flamingos in early spring (Wikivoyage).
Local black Gnaoua music.
Hike the dune

Instead of dropping hundreds of dirham for a remote camping experience with an all so fake looking headscarf, why not just stay on top of the dunes yourself after the sun has set? Bring a sleeping bag, the sand is quite...
From where Merzouga ends in the south it is basically just 5 km straight across the dune from west to east to reach the other side of the dune.
This does not seem to have become a trend yet. Nevertheless, some accommodations have skiers for rent, try Dar Gamra. Otherwise, maybe you are lucky and find a snowboard.

It is also possible to tour the dunes on ATVs. However, it is not as much fun as it might sound at first. You are basically following a guide and can not go bananas with your rented quad. Price per Wikivoyage: From 400 dirham pp for a tour incl. guide (negotiable).

A 2 hour drive that includes a ride with a 4WD onto the dunes, visit to a local village (and probably shop of a cousin), and a visit of the Dayet Srij lake with the impressive dunes in the back. Price per Wikivoyage: 800 dirham per 2 hr (negotiable).

stay: Dune-edge lodges and kasbah-style guesthouses.
Camp: check what is included (dinner, breakfast, transport).

Auberge Sahara Hotel: Clean hotel in an oasis at the edge of the Erg Chebbi sand dunes run by flexible staff. (Wikivoyage listing, edited 2021)

scams.d: Someone offers to guide you for free then leads you to a shop for commission. Official guides carry a badge. Say a firm 'la, shukran' and keep walking.
Common in the Marrakech and Fes medinas. It is a lie to redirect you. Check on your map.
Petit taxis must use the meter. If the driver refuses, wait for another. Agree the full price before moving if there is no meter.
They may say your hotel is closed or that tickets are sold out. Buy tickets only at the official window. CTM and Supratours charge a small luggage fee; do not pay for a bag that fits in the cabin.
Do not let anyone start henna on your hand or put an animal on you without agreeing the price first. Ask before you take photos of performers.
Check the price of drinks before you order, especially on tourist squares.
Offers of hash are everywhere in tourist areas. Drug laws are strict for tourists and these offers are often a scam or police bait. Say no.
Use banks, official exchange offices or ATMs. Count the money. Keep exchange receipts if you want to change dirhams back. Max 2,000 MAD may leave the country (Wikivoyage).

tips: Currency is the dirham (MAD). Carry small notes and coins. Hotels and taxis often have no change.
You cannot buy dirhams outside Morocco. Max 2,000 MAD may leave the country (Wikivoyage).
Do not drink tap water. Bottled water is cheap.
Trains are the best way to travel between the big cities (ONCF). Buy on oncf-voyages.ma, not on re-seller sites with mark-ups (Wikivoyage).
Buy CTM or Supratours bus tickets at the official window.
Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) especially in the medina and in the countryside.
Public displays of affection and same-sex relations are legal risks in Morocco.
Friday lunch is traditional couscous day in many restaurants.
